problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & -2 & -1 \\ -8 & -10 & 12 & 3 \\ 0 & -4 & -3 & -11 \\ 0 & 6 & 24 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ given above, what is the value of ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{34}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the LU Factorization of a 4x4 Matrix
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062864/assets/9129b6fbd360b9b9bcc937fd2acf0aedc25681d4b3dca100be7f681b7bb347dd.png) 

If $A=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ given above, what is the value of $l_{42} \cdot u_{24}?$
examples.worked_solution:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 6 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ -6 & -6 & 9 & -7 \\ 0 & 4 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+1{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 6 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 6 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 6 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & \,2\, & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062864/assets/ac086686e36fdc3e3fffbf4e772f5bdd3d797a71cd06a8e0c4c0bc338051371e.png)

Finally, since $l_{42}=-2$ and $u_{24}=-3,$ we get

$$
l_{42} \cdot u_{24} = (-2) \cdot (-3) =6.
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 \\ -2 & 8 & 12 \\ -6 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $B$ given above, what is the value of ${l}_{31}\cdot {u}_{22}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $B$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 \\ -2 & 8 & 12 \\ -6 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 \\ -1 & 11 & 16 \\ -6 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 \\ -1 & 11 & 16 \\ \,\,-3\,\, & 11 & 8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 \\ -1 & 11 & 16 \\ \,\,-3\,\, & \,\,1\,\, & -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 11 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, since ${l}_{31}=-3$ and ${u}_{22}=11,$ we get

$$
{l}_{31}\cdot {u}_{22}=(-3)\cdot 11=-33.
$$
